name: Prize crossword No 26,645
preamble: Fifteen solutions are of a kind, not further defined.

clue.text: Symptom of cold keeps husband in

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds the other within
kept in means held inside, completing the instruction to enclose

blocks.note: a cough is a common sign of a cold
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone with a cold makes their husband stay indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says fifteen answers are birds with no definition, so the whole clue is wordplay. The chough is a red-billed crow of sea cliffs.
explanation.definitionFit: The chough is a member of the crow family, one of the puzzle's fifteen thematic birds.

clue.text: Female runner

blocks.note: a hen is a female bird
a harrier is a cross-country runner

explanation.surface: A woman athlete, perhaps a sprinter.
explanation.walkthrough: With the definition supplied by the preamble, both words are wordplay; harriers is a common name for running clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The hen harrier is a bird of prey that hunts low over moorland, one of the thematic birds.

clue.text: 1 of 50 garments in a range for uplifting

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up means reading from the bottom upward, so letters run backwards
one thing set inside another means the letters go within

blocks.note: bras are items of underwear
taken as written
ken is range of knowledge, as in 'beyond my ken'

explanation.surface: Underwear sold in a line designed for lift and support.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 of 50' looks like a cross-reference to entry 1, but it is the definition: one of the fifty US states. Ken means knowledge or range of understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebraska is one of the fifty states making up the United States of America.

clue.text: Appropriate to be astride a horse

indicators.note: a rider astride has legs on either side, so one piece straddles the other

blocks.note: to appropriate is to take for oneself
taken as written
H is slang for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: It is fitting to sit on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse and H are both slang names for heroin, a common crossword equivalence. The takahe is a rare flightless bird of New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: The takahe is a large flightless rail found only in New Zealand, one of the thematic birds.

clue.text: What "blonde" means, putting the counter-argument

blocks.note: first meaning: blonde means having light, fair hair
second meaning: the phrase used to introduce a balancing point

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the phrase literally, the infinitive of being fair-haired; the second is the conversational phrase that introduces the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: Speakers say this phrase when conceding a point to the opposing view, and literally it is being light-haired.

clue.text: Rest, relaxing by lake, in thematic film

indicators.note: relaxing loosens things up, so the letters are freed to rearrange
one thing set inside another means these letters go within

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for lake
Kes, the 1969 Ken Loach film about a boy and his kestrel, fits the bird theme

explanation.surface: Taking it easy by a lake while watching a film.
explanation.walkthrough: Kes is a 1969 British film about a working-class boy who trains a kestrel, which is why it is called thematic.
explanation.definitionFit: Kestrels are small falcons that hover over verges, plural here, among the thematic birds.

clue.text: Whisk round a couple of eggs for starters

indicators.note: going round something surrounds it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a beater is a kitchen whisk

blocks.clueFragment: a couple of eggs for starters
blocks.note: the opening letter of eggs, taken twice

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: whisk two eggs to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a recipe step, but 'starters' asks for initial letters, and 'a couple' doubles one.
explanation.definitionFit: The bee-eater is a brightly coloured bird that catches bees and wasps in flight, one of the thematic birds.

clue.text: Drink over a litre

indicators.note: in a down clue, being over means sitting above, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: tea is a drink
L is the abbreviation for a litre

explanation.surface: Someone drinks more than a litre.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble supplies the definition, so every word is wordplay. The teal is a small dabbling duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater duck, one of the fifteen thematic birds in the grid.

clue.text: Dunderhead is not all there

indicators.note: only part of the word is present, so a portion of it is the answer

blocks.note: the middle letters of this word

explanation.surface: A fool is a bit simple, not all there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not all there' is an idiom for being dim, which suits a dunderhead; here it says only some of the word is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird related to the ostrich, one of the thematic birds.

clue.text: A European sun-lover may, do you say?

indicators.note: asking what you say points to how the words are pronounced

blocks.note: someone who loves the sun may lie in it and bask

explanation.surface: A question about whether a European might be a sunbather.
explanation.walkthrough: The Basques are a people of the western Pyrenees, in Spain and France.
explanation.definitionFit: A Basque is a native of the Basque Country, a region straddling northern Spain and south-west France.

clue.text: Righted a wrong in later life

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so these letters need rearranging

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone corrected an old mistake late in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Righted' and 'wrong' sit side by side as opposites, which hides that 'wrong' is the anagram signal acting on 'Righted a'.
explanation.definitionFit: The third age is the period of active retirement after working life, so it names one's later years.

clue.text: Why Imogen constructed this grid is not important

blocks.note: first meaning: the setter built the puzzle around fifteen thematic feathered creatures
second meaning: an idiom for trivial or worthless

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark about why the setter bothered making this puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the theme-revealing clue: read literally, the grid was made for its fifteen avian answers; as an idiom, the phrase means trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, originally American, describes anything worthless or trivial, and literally names whom the grid was built for.

clue.text: Overcoming resistance, move reluctantly to capital

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming over something means sitting above it, so that piece goes last

blocks.note: to budge is to shift slightly, often unwillingly
Riga is the capital of Latvia
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone overcomes their resistance and grudgingly relocates to the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overcoming resistance' reads as beating opposition, but in a down entry it places the rest of the wordplay above R.
explanation.definitionFit: The budgerigar is a small Australian parakeet popular as a cage bird, one of the thematic birds.

clue.text: Who would send such an invoice — it's cobblers!

blocks.clueFragment: Who would send such an invoice
blocks.note: surface reading: asking which trade issues a particular kind of bill
setter's reading: cobblers mend footwear, so their invoice is for footwear; cobblers is also British slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: An indignant customer receives an outrageous invoice and calls it rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' is British slang for nonsense, so the surface is a protest; read literally, shoemakers send this sort of bill, giving the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoebill is a large African wading bird with a huge clog-shaped beak, one of the thematic birds.

clue.text: Get back to work when day breaks

indicators.note: breaking into something means entering it, so one piece forces its way inside

blocks.note: to restart is to begin working again
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Resume your labours at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When day breaks' reads as daybreak, but it means the abbreviation for day breaks into the other word.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird with a flickering rust-red tail, one of the thematic birds.

clue.text: One lawyer looking embarrassed, being rude

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
LLB is a Bachelor of Laws degree
someone embarrassed goes red in the face

explanation.surface: A blushing solicitor is behaving discourteously.
explanation.walkthrough: LLB, the Bachelor of Laws degree, stands for a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone badly brought up lacks manners, so the word describes discourteous or impolite behaviour.

clue.text: Owning collection, I sort out artist

indicators.note: sorting out reorganises things, so these letters are rearranged
to own is to have and hold, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a set is a collection of things

explanation.surface: A painter who owns a collection is told to tidy it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' does double work: it is both fodder and, with 'out', the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Gabriel Rossetti was a Victorian painter and poet, a founder of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood.

clue.text: Book one form of transport with equipment for gardener

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a van is a vehicle
a hoe is a garden tool for weeding

explanation.surface: Reserve a vehicle along with gardening tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb meaning reserve, but it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivanhoe is Sir Walter Scott's 1819 historical novel set in medieval England.

clue.text: Be conscious of the sea, perhaps, aboard ship

indicators.note: being on board means being inside the vessel, so these pieces go within

blocks.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
to hear something is to be aware of it
the sea is an example of water

explanation.surface: A passenger notices the sea while on a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: SS, for steamship, splits to wrap the other pieces; 'perhaps' signals that the sea is one example of the wider word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearwaters are long-winged seabirds that skim low over the waves, plural here, among the thematic birds.

clue.text: Commonly own a complete range — I say!

indicators.note: common speech drops the initial aitch, so the words are pronounced as a casual speaker would
what a speaker says points to the sound of the words rather than their spelling

blocks.note: to own is to have, and a complete range is a set; in casual speech have loses its aitch

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at owning the full collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' marks a dropped H, as in Cockney or other casual British speech, and 'I say!' is also a dated exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a black-and-white wading bird with an upturned bill, the emblem of the RSPB.

clue.text: First in consecutive series

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
a row is a series of things in a line

explanation.surface: The opening item in a run of successive things.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a single phrase, but 'First in' applies only to the next word, and 'series' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The crow is a large black bird of the corvid family, one of the thematic birds.

clue.text: Port is not quite finished

indicators.note: something not quite finished stops just short, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: The English Channel ferry port in Kent

explanation.surface: A harbour development is nearly complete.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover is the major English ferry port facing France across the Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: The dove is a small pigeon, often a symbol of peace, one of the thematic birds.

clue.text: American island is a struggling former colony

indicators.note: something struggling is twisting and writhing, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: Rhode Island is the smallest US state
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American island is a former colony in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like the link between definition and wordplay, but it is fodder alongside 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was a British colony in southern Africa, now Zimbabwe and Zambia, named after Cecil Rhodes.

clue.text: Encouragement to opera singer who took nude role

blocks.note: 'go!' is a shout of encouragement
a diva is a leading female opera singer

explanation.surface: A cheer for an opera star who performed naked on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a modern stage production; the 'role' is the legendary naked ride through Coventry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Godiva, by legend, rode naked through Coventry to protest her husband's taxes on the townspeople.

clue.text: A gun, when packed in clothing

indicators.note: something packed in is put inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: wear means clothes, as in menswear
heat is American slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A weapon smuggled in someone's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Heat is American criminal slang for a firearm, as in 'packing heat', which 'packed' slyly echoes.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small migrant songbird with a white rump, one of the thematic birds.

clue.text: Red Sea and river in France

blocks.note: mer is French for sea
the Lot is a river in south-west France; 'in France' also turns the sea into French

explanation.surface: The Red Sea and a French river are listed together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Sea' reads as one name, but 'Red' is the definition and 'Sea' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Merlot is a dark grape variety and the red wine made from it, notably in Bordeaux.
